context: Introduce the declarative mapping in todo_findings.py and drive the test from validate_blind_spot's own constants by import, never from a hand-copied literal list -- a copied list drifts exactly the way the two parsers already drifted. Include a negative test proving an undeclared field fails, so the guard is proven to fail closed rather than merely passing today.
description:
The root cause of the whole silent-loss class: validate_blind_spot.py accepts one field set (ALLOWED_FIELDS = 5 required + 8 optional) and _split_body parses EVERY '## ' section, but parse_draft (_project/scripts/todo_findings.py) reads a strictly narrower set -- 5 frontmatter keys plus evidence, and only 4 of the parsed sections. The two sets are never compared by any test, so a validator-accepted field silently vanishes and 'todo finding sync' still prints 'synced 1' with no error and no warning. Measured over the live corpus 2026-07-29: 65 of 65 files lose content this way.

The fix is a fail-closed contract, not a one-off patch: declare the parser's field and section homes machine-readably in todo_findings.py (for example FIELD_HOMES and SECTION_HOMES mappings), and test that every name in validate_blind_spot.ALLOWED_FIELDS and every known body heading has a declared home. Fields not yet given a real column carry an explicit, named pending set so the contract is still total -- adding a NEW validator field without a home fails the test immediately, and findings-schema-v4-lossless-legacy-fields empties the pending set rather than editing the assertion.

This is the guard that stops the class recurring; it is deliberately independent of the v4 migration so it can land first and make the v4 work verifiable.

anti_patterns.dont: Assert against a hand-copied list of field names in the test
anti_patterns.instead: import validate_blind_spot and derive the expected set from its own constants at test time
anti_patterns.why: a duplicated literal drifts from validate_blind_spot.ALLOWED_FIELDS exactly the way parse_draft already drifted from it -- that drift is the defect being fixed

anti_patterns.instead: give the module-level pytestmark 'unit' and 'medium', and confirm with uv run -- python _project/scripts/timing_policy_check.py
anti_patterns.why: the fast-lane cap in _project/config/fast_test_lane_policy.json has near-zero headroom on develop and CI's timing_policy_check --strict trips on any fast-lane addition

anti_patterns.dont: Silence the gap by adding the unmapped fields to an unnamed skip list or by loosening the assertion
anti_patterns.instead: name the pending set explicitly and require every entry to be justified, so v4 empties it and any new field still fails closed
anti_patterns.why: an unnamed exemption hides the very loss the guard exists to surface and makes the phase-5 parity gate unfalsifiable again

preserves.behavior: parse_draft's current return shape and behaviour for the fields it already handles
todo finding sync stays credential-free for create and candidates and unchanged for already-landed drafts

verifications.description: findings script tests pass, including the new completeness guard
the fast-lane timing policy still holds after adding the test module
verifications.expected: exit 0; the new module is unit+medium, not fast
